title: Охота на Вику и браслет Саши  (Pursuing Vika and Sasha's Bracelet)

segments.t: Peering through the office window into the dining room, Aleksandr asks Max whether art director Vika is seeing anyone and immediately sets his sights on her. Moments later, Vika steps in to tell the new chef that guests are waiting to greet him, while Sasha shows off her bracelet at the bar.
Слушай, а вот это, Луи, с кем?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Слушай, а вот это, Луи, с кем?
'Listen, who is Louis over there with?' Vika quizzes bluntly while looking straight at Louis here.

'Come on, I am just kidding.' Max lightly gives this word of agreement in one quick breath using "ladno" ("alright") — built from the old Russian root for harmony and order, used every day for "okay, fine".
'And what about our director?' Checking on the head teacher at once, Louis keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Vika purely through rising pitch.
'She does not seem to be with anyone.' Vika speaks up dryly without holding back, to clear the air between them once and for all.
'You do not say.' Max naturally gives this direct affirmation to Vika using "da" ("yes") — a crisp "da" ("yes") that confirms the point without extra words.
'Actually, the guests were asking for you.' Checking on the visitors on the spot, Louis drops in "voobshche" ("in general, altogether") to sum up the whole situation at once.
'Tell them for me.' Vika counters evenly watching Louis, testing Louis's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
'No, no, not right now.' Turning firmly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'It is my first day at the restaurant.' Talking about the restaurant during the talk, Louis links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Well, how could anyone say no to me?' Vika asks firmly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
'This is already the third bracelet.' Discussing the tag with Vika, Max uses "braslet" ("the tag") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'Do you see this right here?' Holding firm quietly beside Vika, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.

'All right, I am going to get back to work.' Vika casually drops this word of agreement with Louis using "ladno" ("alright") — built from the old Russian root for harmony and order, used every day for "okay, fine".
Слушай, а вот это, Луи, с кем?
That wraps up this scene as aleksandr sets his sights on art director Vika after learning she is single, while Sasha shows off a new bracelet at the bar. Until next time!
